key_insight: Federated learning across LEO orbital planes using HAPS as aggregators enables efficient, privacy-preserving beam selection; topology-aware GNNs can better capture spatial relationships and often outperform MLPs in dynamic NTN conditions.
problem_solved: Efficient beam management in LEO Non-Terrestrial Networks under rapidly changing propagation and strict inter-node communication/privacy constraints, avoiding costly centralized data collection.
method: Model orbital planes as distributed learners and use High-Altitude Platform Stations (HAPS) for federated aggregation to limit raw-data transfer.
Train and compare two local models — an MLP baseline and a Graph Neural Network (GNN) that encodes spatial/topological relations — using realistic channel and beamforming datasets.
Evaluate trade-offs in selection accuracy, communication overhead, and adaptability to LEO mobility and propagation dynamics.
impact: Provides a scalable, communication-efficient approach for 6G NTN beam management that preserves data locality; ML practitioners can adopt FL+GNN designs to improve topology-aware decisions while reducing central coordination and data-sharing requirements.
visual_elements: System diagram: LEO satellites organized by orbital plane, HAPS aggregators, and ground/UEs to show the FL topology.
Federated workflow flowchart: local training on-orbit → model upload to HAPS → aggregation → global model broadcast.
Comparison chart (bars/lines): MLP vs GNN on metrics like beam-selection accuracy, convergence speed, and communication overhead (qualitative or relative).
Spatio-temporal heatmap: beam coverage/selection over time illustrating adaptive steering under dynamic channel conditions.
paper_title: Federated Learning-driven Beam Management in LEO 6G Non-Terrestrial Networks
paper_authors: Maria Lamprini Bartsioka, Ioannis A. Bartsiokas, Athanasios D. Panagopoulos, Dimitra I. Kaklamani, Iakovos S. Venieris
